title: Conveyor will not start after panel maintenance
summary: The conveyor worked yesterday. After the operator panel was serviced, pressing Start does nothing. Find the root cause from evidence, repair it and prove the system works.
objectives: Compare what the PLC sees with what the field device does
Use the input LEDs and a voltage measurement to locate a fault
Explain why a normally closed Stop button is used
instructions: Start the simulation. The PLC is already in RUN with the program that worked before the maintenance.
Reproduce the symptom: press Start and watch the motor, the PLC inputs and the module LEDs.
Collect evidence: watch the input image, look at the digital input LEDs and measure the terminal voltages.
Submit the root cause you can prove, apply the repair, then run Check to verify the repaired system.
hints: Look at every input the start logic depends on, not only StartPB.
A normally closed contact delivers 24 V while the button is NOT pressed. What does the Stop input show?
Measure the Stop input terminal with the button released.

scenarios.title: Start and stop the repaired conveyor

criteria.title: Start energizes the contactor
criteria.onFail: The contactor still does not switch on after Start.

criteria.title: The conveyor keeps running
criteria.onFail: The conveyor does not keep running after Start is released.

criteria.title: Stop still works
criteria.onFail: Stop no longer stops the conveyor. A repair must keep the Stop function safe.

troubleshooting.symptom: Pressing Start does nothing: the conveyor motor and the run lamp stay off. No alarm is shown. The panel was serviced this morning.

diagnosisOptions.label: The Start button contact does not close
The Stop button contact block was replaced by a normally open block
The motor overload relay has tripped
The digital input module has failed
The PLC program contains a logic error

repairs.label: Fit a normally closed contact block to the Stop button

debrief.rootCause: During the panel service the Stop button received a normally open contact block instead of a normally closed one. The program expects StopPB to be TRUE while Stop is not pressed, so it saw a permanent stop command.
evidence: StopPB was FALSE with nobody touching the Stop button, and became TRUE only while Stop was pressed: the opposite of the documented behavior.
StartPB did become TRUE when Start was pressed, so the start circuit and the input module were working.
MotorContactor never went TRUE, so the signal was blocked inside the logic by the stop condition, not lost on the way to the contactor.
No alarm and no module diagnostic were present, which points away from hardware failures and toward a wrong field device.
debrief.repair: Fit a normally closed contact block to the Stop button, then verify that Start, run and Stop behave as before the service.
debrief.reasoning: Compare every input with what its documentation says it should be at rest. A stop circuit is normally closed so that a broken wire stops the machine; an input that is FALSE at rest and TRUE when operated has the wrong contact type.
